themes.name: Agentic AI in research
themes.description: Focuses on AI agents capable of performing complex research tasks autonomously, often described as acting independently or with minimal human oversight.

themes.name: AI coding assistants
themes.description: Covers AI tools and techniques designed to help developers write, debug, and optimize code, often functioning as intelligent co-pilots.

themes.name: AI research tools
themes.description: Articles discussing AI-powered platforms, software, and suites specifically built to aid in various research activities, from data analysis to literature review.

themes.name: AI chatbot research
themes.description: Explores the development, capabilities, limitations, and impact of AI chatbots, particularly in conversational and interactive contexts.

themes.name: AI testing automation
themes.description: Covers the application of AI in automating various testing processes, including software quality assurance, security testing, and operational validation.

themes.name: AI workforce impact
themes.description: Examines how AI is affecting jobs, skills, hiring, and the overall labor market, including concerns about job displacement and the emergence of new roles.

themes.name: AI research platform
themes.description: Focuses on AI platforms designed to integrate various research functionalities, enabling more efficient and comprehensive research workflows.

themes.name: AI design research
themes.description: Discusses how AI is being used in the design process, from generating design concepts to aiding in user interface and product design research.

themes.name: AI sentiment feedback
themes.description: Covers the use of AI to analyze and interpret user sentiment from reviews, feedback, and other textual data.

themes.name: AI product research
themes.description: Focuses on AI applications for market research, understanding product performance, identifying opportunities, and informing product development.

note: Themes identified by analyzing articles from curated sources, Google News, HackerNews, and DEV.to this month.
